title: Gentamicin Bladder Instillation on CAUTI
official: A Randomized Controlled Trial to Evaluate the Effectiveness of Gentamicin Bladder Instillation on CAUTI
summary: Urinary tract infections in catheterized patients is an unacceptable complication and has been termed a 'never event' by the Center for Medicare \& Medicaid Services (CMS); however there is not consensus among clinicians on how to best prevent CAUTIs. We propose a prospective randomized controlled trial to test the efficacy of prophylactic gentamicin bladder irrigation in elimination of CAUTIs.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. age greater than 18
2. admitted with a trauma, surgical, or neuro-critical care diagnosis
3. indwelling foley catheter in place

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Documented positive UA or Urine Culture within the past 7 days or upon admission
2. Traumatic bladder injury
3. Gross hematuria
4. Chronic indwelling urethral or chronic suprapubic foley catheter
5. allergy to gentamicin or similar aminoglycosides
